instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Hi there! I’m having an issue with my phone—it’s been showing ‘No Service’ for the past few hours. Can you help me get it working again?
I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, customer ID, or your full name and date of birth?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more information.

Thank you for providing your information. I’ve identified your account and found the line associated with your phone number (555-123-2002). 

Let’s start troubleshooting your “No Service” issue. Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know if you see any icons such as Airplane Mode, signal bars, or any other indicators? This will help me determine the next steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I checked my phone’s status bar, and I see the Airplane Mode icon is on. There aren’t any signal bars showing—just the airplane symbol and the battery indicator. What should I do next?

The Airplane Mode being on is the reason you’re seeing “No Service.” Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once it’s off, wait a few moments to see if your signal bars return and if your service is restored. Let me know if you see your signal come back or if you still have issues after turning Airplane Mode off.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode, but I still don’t see any signal bars. The status bar now shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” What should I try next?

Thank you for the update. Since Airplane Mode is off but you still see “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” the next step is to check your SIM card status. 

Please check your phone’s SIM card status and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” This will help us determine if there’s an issue with your SIM card.
The SIM card is locked with a PIN code.
It looks like my SIM card is locked with a PIN code. What should I do to unlock it?

Since your SIM card is locked with a PIN code, you’ll need to enter the correct PIN to unlock it. If you’re unsure of your PIN or have entered it incorrectly multiple times, your SIM may become locked with a PUK code, which requires additional steps.

For security reasons, I’m unable to provide or reset SIM PIN/PUK codes directly. I recommend checking any documentation from your carrier or the original SIM card packaging for your default PIN. If you don’t have this information or are unable to unlock your SIM, you’ll need to contact technical support for further assistance.

Would you like me to transfer you to a human agent who can help you with unlocking your SIM card?
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent who can help with unlocking my SIM card. Thank you!
